The built-in minimal app permissions granted unrestricted `read` access to the `directus_settings` singleton. As a
result, any authenticated user with `app_access: true` and no custom permissions could read every settings field,
including server-side AI and MCP configuration that is intended to be admin-only.

The highest impact field is `ai_openai_compatible_headers`, which stores the custom request headers used to authenticate
against a self-configured OpenAI-compatible backend. Unlike the provider API key fields, this field is not encrypted or
concealed, so any bearer token or API key an administrator placed there was returned in plaintext.

## Impact

A user whose only privilege is app access could read, among others:

- `ai_openai_compatible_headers`: plaintext authorization headers for the configured OpenAI-compatible backend
- `ai_openai_compatible_base_url`: internal or private endpoint of that backend
- `ai_system_prompt`: server-side AI system prompt
- `mcp_system_prompt`: server-side MCP system prompt

The data was reachable through both the REST (`/settings`) and GraphQL (`/graphql/system`) system endpoints, since both
resolve through the same permission layer.

Where `ai_openai_compatible_headers` contained credentials, the disclosure is a usable secret rather than inert
configuration: the value was confirmed to authenticate successfully against a backend that required it. This can lead to
unauthorized use of, and billing against, the customer's AI provider account, and it discloses the internal endpoint
that backend is hosted on.

The encrypted provider key fields (`ai_openai_api_key`, `ai_openai_compatible_api_key`) were correctly masked and are
not disclosed.

Impact is reduced to disclosure of AI and MCP prompt text plus backend metadata on instances where
`ai_openai_compatible_headers` is unset or holds no credential material. Prompt disclosure itself may still reveal
operational or tenant-specific detail.

Exploitation requires a valid, non-admin account on the instance. No user interaction, no custom `directus_settings`
permission, and no additional privilege is needed.

### Note for existing installations

The patch changes the built-in minimal app permissions. In versions before 12.3.0, the policy creation dialog in the
Data Studio also wrote app access permission rows into the database, so policies created that way may retain a stored
`directus_settings` read permission with no field restriction, which still exposes all fields after upgrading.
Administrators should review existing policies for an unrestricted `directus_settings` read permission and remove or
field-restrict it. Directus 12.3.0 stops the dialog from persisting these rows
([directus/directus#28101](https://github.com/directus/directus/pull/28101)).

## Workarounds

For instances that cannot upgrade immediately:

- Remove credentials from `ai_openai_compatible_headers` and rotate any value that was stored there, since it must be
  assumed disclosed to every app user.
- Avoid placing sensitive content in `ai_system_prompt` and `mcp_system_prompt`.

## Credits

Reported by @kamil-sawicki
